knowledge-base.name: devops
knowledge-base.triggers: CI/CD, pipeline, Docker, container, deployment, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, infrastructure, Terraform, Kubernetes, helm, rollback, blue-green, canary, rolling update, IaC, secrets, build, artifact, registry, staging, environment, health check, readiness probe
knowledge-base.overview: DevOps practices for reliable, automated, and secure software delivery. The goal is fast feedback loops, reproducible environments, and the ability to deploy and roll back with confidence at any time.

cicd-pipeline-design.principle: Pipelines are the deployment contract — everything that reaches production must pass through them.

stages.stage: Fastest checks first: syntax, style, SAST. Block on any finding.
Isolated, no network/DB. Parallelized by module.
Compile, bundle, create Docker image. Produce immutable artifact.
SAST, dependency audit, container scan, secret scan.
Tests with real dependencies (DB, cache). Use service containers.
Automated deploy to staging. Run smoke tests.
Gated by staging pass. Blue-green or canary.

caching.rule: Cache dependency installs (node_modules, pip, Maven) keyed on lock file hash
Cache Docker layer builds using buildx cache-from/cache-to
Cache build artifacts between stages using pipeline artifacts, not re-building

artifact-management.rule: Every build produces one immutable artifact tagged with git SHA
Never rebuild the artifact for different environments — promote the same image
Store artifacts in a registry (Docker Hub, ECR, Artifact Registry) with retention policy

parallelization.rule: Run independent test suites in parallel matrix jobs
Split slow test suites across shards using matrix strategy
Lint, unit test, and security scan can all run concurrently after checkout

multi-stage-builds.principle: Use multi-stage builds to minimize final image size and attack surface
multi-stage-builds.code-example:
# Stage 1: Build FROM node:20-alpine AS builder WORKDIR /app COPY package*.json ./ RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . . RUN npm run build
# Stage 2: Runtime (lean image) FROM node:20-alpine AS runtime WORKDIR /app RUN addgroup -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -G appgroup COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules USER appuser EXPOSE 3000 HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 CMD wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1 CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

layer-optimization.rule: Copy dependency manifests and install before copying source — maximizes layer cache reuse
Combine RUN commands with && to reduce layer count
Use .dockerignore to exclude node_modules, .git, test files, docs
Pin base image versions (node:20.11-alpine3.19, not node:latest)

security.rule: Run as non-root user — create a dedicated service account in the image
Use distroless or Alpine base images to minimize CVE surface
Scan images with Trivy or Snyk before pushing to registry
Never bake secrets into image layers — inject at runtime via env or mounted secrets
Use read-only filesystem where possible (--read-only with tmpfs mounts)

compose-patterns.rule: Use Docker Compose for local dev parity — mirrors production service topology
Use named volumes for persistent data, not bind mounts in production
Define health checks so dependent services wait for readiness
compose-patterns.code-example:
services: api: build: . depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy environment: DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL} # injected, never hardcoded healthcheck: test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:3000/health"] interval: 30s timeout: 5s retries: 3
db: image: postgres:16-alpine healthcheck: test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"] interval: 10s timeout: 5s retries: 5

workflow-syntax.rule: Use reusable workflows (.github/workflows/reusable-*.yml) for shared logic across repos
Use composite actions for multi-step logic reused within a repo
Pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, not a tag (security: prevents tag mutation)
Set minimal permissions at the workflow and job level with permissions: key

secrets-management.rule: Store secrets in GitHub Secrets (repo or org level), never in workflow files
Use environment-scoped secrets for staging/prod separation
Use OIDC (openid-connect) for cloud credentials — no long-lived keys needed
secrets-management.code-example: # OIDC-based AWS credential (no long-lived keys) - name: Configure AWS credentials uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4 with: role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/github-actions-deploy aws-region: us-east-1

matrix-builds.code-example: jobs: test: strategy: matrix: node-version: [18, 20, 22] os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }} cache: 'npm' - run: npm ci && npm test

caching.code-example: - uses: actions/cache@v4 with: path: ~/.npm key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }} restore-keys: | ${{ runner.os }}-node-

github-actions.full-pipeline-example:
name: CI/CD Pipeline
on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: branches: [main]
permissions: contents: read id-token: write # for OIDC
jobs: lint-and-test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: '20' cache: 'npm' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm test -- --coverage
security-scan: runs-on: ubuntu-latest needs: lint-and-test steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: npm audit --audit-level=high - uses: github/codeql-action/init@v3 with: languages: javascript - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v3
build-and-push: runs-on: ubuntu-latest needs: [lint-and-test, security-scan] if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Build Docker image run: docker build -t myapp:${{ github.sha }} . - name: Scan image uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master with: image-ref: myapp:${{ github.sha }} exit-code: '1' severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH' - name: Push to registry run: | echo ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }} | docker login -u ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_USER }} --password-stdin docker push myapp:${{ github.sha }}
deploy-staging: runs-on: ubuntu-latest needs: build-and-push environment: staging steps: - name: Deploy to staging run: ./scripts/deploy.sh staging ${{ github.sha }} - name: Smoke test run: ./scripts/smoke-test.sh https://staging.example.com
deploy-production: runs-on: ubuntu-latest needs: deploy-staging environment: production steps: - name: Deploy to production (canary) run: ./scripts/deploy.sh production ${{ github.sha }} --strategy=canary

strategy.name: blue-green
strategy.description: Two identical environments (blue=current, green=new). Switch traffic atomically after validation.
strategy.when-to-use: Zero-downtime required, easy rollback is priority, stateless services

steps.step: Deploy new version to idle environment (green)
Run health checks and smoke tests on green
Switch load balancer to send 100% traffic to green
Monitor error rates for defined window (e.g., 15 minutes)
If healthy: decommission blue. If not: switch back to blue in seconds.

strategy.rollback: Switch load balancer back to blue environment — seconds to complete

strategy.name: canary
strategy.description: Route a small percentage of traffic (1-10%) to the new version. Gradually increase if healthy.
strategy.when-to-use: Want to validate with real traffic before full rollout, higher-risk changes

steps.step: Deploy new version alongside old version
Route 1-5% of traffic to new version
Monitor error rate, latency, and business metrics
Increment traffic: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% on schedule or auto
Rollback if metrics exceed thresholds at any increment

strategy.rollback: Route 0% traffic to new version, scale it down
strategy.code-example: # Kubernetes canary with Argo Rollouts spec: strategy: canary: steps: - setWeight: 5 - pause: {duration: 10m} - setWeight: 25 - pause: {duration: 10m} - setWeight: 50 - pause: {duration: 10m} analysis: templates: - templateName: error-rate args: - name: service-name value: my-service

strategy.name: rolling
strategy.description: Replace instances of the old version one at a time (or in batches).
strategy.when-to-use: Kubernetes default, when blue-green cost is prohibitive, stateful services

considerations.item: Old and new versions run concurrently — API must be backward compatible
Rollback is slower than blue-green (must roll back each instance)

strategy.name: feature-flags
strategy.description: Deploy code dark (disabled), enable for specific users or percentage without re-deploying.
strategy.when-to-use: Decouple deploy from release, A/B testing, gradual feature rollout
strategy.rule: Feature flag state is config, not code — never gate on hardcoded user IDs

terraform.principle: Infrastructure state is truth — all resources managed in code, no console drift.

state-management.rule: Store state in remote backend (S3 + DynamoDB lock, GCS, Terraform Cloud)
Never commit terraform.tfstate to version control
Use workspaces or separate state files per environment

module-patterns.rule: Create reusable modules for repeated patterns (VPC, ECS service, RDS instance)
Output values needed by dependent modules explicitly

workflow.step: terraform apply tfplan — apply only the reviewed plan

rules.rule: Never hardcode secrets in source code, IaC, or pipeline files
Never log secrets — mask or redact before any output
Never pass secrets in URLs or query strings
Use different secrets per environment — no shared prod/staging credentials
Rotate secrets regularly; use short-lived credentials (OIDC, instance roles) where possible
Audit secret access — log who accessed what and when

injection-patterns.pattern: Standard for 12-factor apps. Injected by orchestrator (ECS task def, K8s Secret, GitHub Secrets).
HashiCorp Vault agent injects secrets as files or env vars at runtime. Supports dynamic secrets with TTL.
Reference ARN in ECS task definition; AWS injects at container start. Rotates automatically with Lambda.
Base64-encoded, mounted as env vars or files. Use Sealed Secrets or External Secrets Operator for GitOps.

secrets-management.tools: HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager, Doppler

environment-management.parity-principle: dev, staging, and prod use the same Docker image, same IaC modules, different config only.

config-separation.rule: Environment-specific config via environment variables, not code branches
Use a config file per environment (terraform.tfvars.staging, .env.staging) — never committed with secrets
Feature flags and scaling counts are the main legitimate differences between environments

promotion-flow.step: Code merged to main → auto-deploy to dev
Staging passes + manual gate → deploy to production

caching-strategies.strategy: Key on lock file (package-lock.json, Pipfile.lock). Saves 1-3 min per build.
Use --cache-from previous build or BuildKit registry cache.
Tools like Nx, Turborepo, Bazel detect changed packages and only rebuild affected.
Cache test results when source files haven't changed (Nx, Bazel).

parallel-builds.rule: Lint, unit tests, and security scans can all run in parallel after checkout
Split test suite by module or file count across matrix shards
Docker multi-platform builds (amd64, arm64) should run in parallel

targets.target: Main branch full pipeline: under 15 minutes
Any step over 10 minutes: investigate for parallelization or caching opportunity

liveness-probe.description: Is the process alive? If this fails, Kubernetes restarts the container.
liveness-probe.rule: Should be cheap — just check if the process can respond, not full dependency chain

readiness-probe.description: Is the service ready to accept traffic? If this fails, remove from load balancer rotation.
readiness-probe.rule: Check actual dependencies (DB connection, cache, external APIs) — if any are down, return 503
readiness-probe.example: GET /ready → 200 if all dependencies healthy, 503 with {"status": "degraded", "checks": {...}} if not

graceful-shutdown.rule: Listen for SIGTERM — stop accepting new requests, finish in-flight requests, then exit
Set terminationGracePeriodSeconds in Kubernetes to allow drain window (default 30s, tune to p99 request latency)

health-checks-readiness.kubernetes-config-example:
livenessProbe: httpGet: path: /health port: 3000 initialDelaySeconds: 10 periodSeconds: 30 failureThreshold: 3
readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /ready port: 3000 initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 10 failureThreshold: 3
lifecycle: preStop: exec: command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"] # allow LB to drain before SIGTERM

deployment-markers.rule: Emit a deploy event to your monitoring platform on every production deployment
Include: service name, version/SHA, environment, deployer, timestamp
deployment-markers.tools: Datadog deploy tracking, New Relic deployments, Grafana annotations, PagerDuty change events
deployment-markers.code-example: # Post deployment marker to Datadog curl -X POST "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/events" \ -H "DD-API-KEY: ${DD_API_KEY}" \ -d '{ "title": "Deployed my-api v'"${VERSION}"'", "text": "SHA: '"${GIT_SHA}"' by '"${DEPLOYER}"'", "tags": ["env:production", "service:my-api", "version:'"${VERSION}"'"] }'

post-deploy-monitoring.rule: Watch error rate for 15 minutes post-deploy before marking deploy complete
Compare p99 latency against pre-deploy baseline — alert if >20% regression
Canary deployments should have automated rollback triggers based on SLO breach

slo-awareness.rule: Define SLOs before deploying: error budget, latency targets, availability target
Burn rate alerts should fire before the deploy window is fully rolled out
Track deployment frequency and mean time to recovery (MTTR) as DORA metrics

devops-checklist.summary: Apply before every pipeline or infra change
devops-checklist.check: No secrets in code, pipeline YAML, logs, or image layers
Health checks and readiness probes configured
Security scanning gates (SAST, deps, container) in pipeline
Dependency and image versions pinned (no :latest in prod)
Deploy event emitted to monitoring platform
IaC formatted and validated (terraform fmt && validate)
